description: pyHMT2D is a Python package from the PSU Environmental Fluid Dynamics repository for controlling two-dimensional hydraulic models and processing their results. It supplies interfaces to SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D, together with a simple backwater demonstration model. Functions read hydraulic results into NumPy arrays, export VTK, sample flow fields and transfer HEC-RAS meshes, boundary conditions and Manning roughness to SRH-2D. Python scripts, command-line examples and optional MCP tools support repeated runs, calibration and Monte Carlo experiments. Spatial extent, mesh resolution and simulation periods come from the user's hydraulic project; this is not a fixed geographic dataset. The package is public and free under MIT. Hydraulic executables must be obtained separately under their own terms. Windows is the main supported environment, with limited Linux support; the README reports development with HEC-RAS 6.6 and SMS 13.4.11, not compatibility with every version. The tool helps prepare and compare flood simulations around infrastructure. It directly controls the catalogue's HEC-RAS model (model-hec-ras); neither execution nor numerical agreement was tested during this metadata review.
